Total domestic production in MY 1979 was assumed to be 1 million vehicles of which 52.6 percent were GM, 27.9 percent were Ford, 16.3 percent were Chrysler, and 3.7 percent were AMC. Additionally, it was assumed that GM and Ford would each sell 50,000 captive imports in MY 1979.

A. Water Quality and Water Supply: Water quality and industrial water supply demand will be impacted by changes in the use of steel, cast iron, aluminum, and plastics in the manufacture of NPA's. The agency expects that the use of steel and cast iron could decrease as a result of weight reduction and CID reduction.
The agency expects that the use of aluminum and plastics could increase as these materials are substituted for iron and steel for purposes of reducing total vehicle weight.
From the viewpoint that all impacts of improving fuel economy from MY 1976 levels to a level where all manufacturers can meet the proposed AFES are attributable to the AFES, the total savings in cast iron and steel would be approximately 42 million pounds. From the viewpoint that only those impacts resulting from actions by GM and Chrysler to meet the AFES over and above their voluntary plans for MY 1979 are attributable to the standard, the total savings in cast iron and steel would be 24.8
